findings.reason: by the item's rule and the review's own prior standard (§2/§3 each state their added constant "retires nothing, because…"), §5 must state that the two flags extend the existing public function and retire nothing (sensor visibility is a new capability) and say whether the MCP animate view is deliberately left behind, which is a one-line text change to §5.
findings.text: §5 grows the public signature of the exported `animate_pulse` (`imas_ink/__init__.py:49`) with `show_probes` and `show_flux_loops`; its text ("No other parameter changes") bounds how many it adds but names no retirement, while the sibling MCP `geometry_figure` tool already carries both flags (`imas_ink/server/mcp.py:232`) and the MCP `animate_pulse` tool of the same capability does not (`imas_ink/server/mcp.py:351`), leaving the two surfaces divergent with no stated disposition

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; §5 adds two keyword arguments to the existing `animate_pulse`, and §1–§4 extended existing interfaces, so no complexity is spread across new wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — `animate_pulse` remains the single animation owner and §5 adds no parallel path; the landed §1–§4 extend single owners (`extract_vessel_shells`, `InkStyle`, `geometry_figure_mpl`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §5 adds two keyword arguments to the exported `animate_pulse` without the "retires nothing, because…" accounting that §2 and §3 carry for their added style constants.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §5 reuses `equilibrium_figure_mpl`'s existing `show_probes`/`show_flux_loops` flags (`imas_ink/figures.py:329-330`) instead of adding drawing, and the landed §1–§4 extend `extract_vessel_shells`, `WallOutline`, `geometry_figure_mpl`'s `ax` and the `InkStyle` fields in place.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §5 extends `animate_pulse` in place, which is the honest change, rather than adding a layer over machinery it could extend.
